title: Main purpose: what a study or mechanism shows
subtitle: Text Structure and Purpose · 25 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **25 of the official questions in Text Structure and Purpose are this one** — 7 Easy, 10 Medium, 8 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The text walks through a method, experiment, or process (researchers did A, measured B, found C, or 'when X happens, Y happens').
- The question asks for the main purpose, and choices mix 'to describe an experiment that...' or 'to explain how X works' with comparisons or evaluations.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Decide whether the text only reports (describe or explain) or also evaluates (criticize, question).
- 2) Check what the choice claims about the result: does it say the study answered a question, raised a new one, or supported a hypothesis?
- Confirm that against the last sentence.
- 3) For process texts, pick the choice that names the whole mechanism, not one step or a comparison.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: A choice correctly says 'describes an experiment' but misstates the result, for example saying the question went unresolved when the text gives clear results.
Or a choice claims the text compares two things when only one is explained.
Read the whole choice, not just its opening verb.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
A choice correctly says 'describes an experiment' but misstates the result, for example saying the question went unresolved when the text gives clear results.
Or a choice claims the text compares two things when only one is explained.
